AITA for telling my wife off for having her mom in the room when she was giving birth | My wife and I agreed from the beginning that we would be the only people in the room when she was going through labor/birth. Her mother and I also don’t get along very well, and neither of us wanted that stress the day of. There was an issue and I was late getting to the hospital, not by a ton though. There was still 3+ hours of labor until the baby came. However, by the time I got there, my wife had called her mother and told her to come. It caused a lot of tension and made the process pretty uncomfortable for me, and thus made it harder to support my wife. We didn’t get that special one on one time with the baby either (we initially planned on having a full day of just us, but it ended up only being a few hours) and I’m really upset about it. It’s been a few weeks and my wife asked me why I am so moody about the topic of the birth, and I exploded at her for violating the plan that we had from the beginning. She cried and blamed me for being late and then told me she wouldn’t discuss it further because I had yelled. AITA here??

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I would say 1 (You Are The Asshole) in this scenario. Here's why: While it's understandable that you felt upset and frustrated about your wife's decision to have her mother in the room during labor, your reaction was disproportionate and hurtful. You had agreed on a plan, but your wife was in a vulnerable and stressful situation, and she made a decision that she thought was best for her at the time. Your lateness, although not extreme, may have contributed to your wife's decision to call her mother. It's possible that she felt anxious or scared and wanted her mother's support. Instead of being understanding and empathetic, you exploded at your wife, making her feel guilty and defensive. It's also important to consider the power dynamics at play. Your wife was in labor, and you were not. She was in a physically and emotionally vulnerable state, and you should have been more supportive and understanding. Additionally, your insistence on having a "special one on one time" with the baby, while understandable, may have been unrealistic. The birth of a child is a significant event, and it's natural for family members to want to be involved. Your wife's decision to have her mother present may have been a way of sharing this experience with her loved one. Your reaction, however, has caused harm and tension in your relationship. By yelling at your wife and making her feel guilty, you've created a situation where she feels uncomfortable discussing the issue further. This could lead to unresolved feelings and resentment, which can be damaging to your relationship. In hindsight, it would have been better to have a calm and empathetic conversation with your wife about your feelings and concerns. You could have expressed your disappointment and frustration in a non-accusatory way, and worked together to find a resolution.
